text: If this happens tonight... you won't make it three days.
One explosion on the sun... and every light in the world goes out at once.
This isn't a movie. It almost happened... and it can happen again, any day.
Nine o'clock at night. You're watching your phone, just like this... then suddenly, nothing.
No lights. No signal.
A solar storm. Billions of tons of fire from the sun... straight at Earth.
Day one. No internet. You can't reach your family.
The ATMs are dead. Your money is locked inside.
Day two. The food is rotting. Every store is closed.
Then the water stops. Electricity was running that too.
Day three. Everything runs out. This is where the chaos starts.
In hospitals, the last generators are keeping patients alive.
Day seven. The world is silent... but you can see every star.
But here's the scarier part.
In 1859, telegraph wires caught fire, and the northern lights reached the Caribbean.
In 1989, six million people in Quebec lost power.
In 2012, a storm just as strong... missed us by nine days.
